title: Pauri 6, sound: teerath naavaa

cards: At Haridwar on the Ganges, people step down the ghats at dawn into cold water. Other rivers and lakes draw people too, someone come to wash off a hard year.
The janamsakhis, the old stories of Guru Nanak's life, say he walked to places like these.
The sixth pauri of Japji opens on the riverbank, with a line about bathing, and its first line rings: two words that rhyme, side by side, like two feet stepping into water.

teach.b: The opening line: teerath naavaa, je tis bhaavaa. Teerath: TEE-rath. A teerath is a pilgrimage place, a holy ford, a spot on a river where people bathe.
Naavaa: NAA-vaa, I would bathe. Je: jay, if. Tis: tiss, to Him.
Bhaavaa: BHAA-vaa, I were pleasing. I would bathe at the holy place, if I were pleasing to Him.
Hear the rhyme: naavaa, bhaavaa, the two halves landing on the same sound, like an echo. Then the line goes on: vin bhaane ki naae karee. Vin: without.
Bhaane: pleasing. Ki: what. Naae karee: bathing would I do.
Without pleasing Him, what bathing would I do? That opens tomorrow. Today, the music.
Guru Nanak builds this pauri from rhyme and repetition, easy to carry in your head.
One line holds a string of treasures: ratan, javaahar, maanik, jewels, gems and rubies; you can hear their weight just in the sound.
And the refrain from pauri five comes back: guraa ik dehi bujhaaee, O Guru, give me this one understanding.
When a refrain repeats, it's telling you what to hold onto: two pauris in a row end on the same request.

how: The sixth pauri of Japji is recited each morning; like the fifth, it ends with the refrain asking the Guru for one understanding, that there is one Giver of all.

games.q: match the sound to its sense.
p: a holy ford, a pilgrimage place

s: the two halves of the line land on the same sound, like an echo.
the refrain from pauri five never comes back
guraa ik dehi bujhaaee returns in pauri six.
it's a pilgrimage place, a holy ford where people bathe.

games.q: the first line says I would bathe at the holy place, on one condition. what is it?
o: if I were pleasing to Him.
games.why: je tis bhaavaa: if I were pleasing to Him.

practice: Say it slowly, out loud if you can, and let the rhyme ring: teerath naavaa, je tis bhaavaa. Say it twice more, softly, and if you know it by heart by now, add the refrain, guraa ik dehi bujhaaee.
Then sit, picture cool water around your feet, and breathe; if you pray, you can rest in Waheguru.

wordCard.voice: Ratan. A jewel: one of the treasures, ratan, javaahar, maanik, that ring through this pauri's sound, which opens teerath naavaa, I would bathe at the holy place.

orig.note: Gurmukhi: the opening of Japji's sixth pauri, Ang 2.

carryVoice: Your line: teerath naavaa. Naavaa, bhaavaa: two halves of the line, landing on one sound. Until tomorrow.
